newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU, Asia pressed on human rights in Singapore.
newsitem.headline: EU, Asia pressed on human rights in Singapore.

text.p: A human rights group on Sunday urged European Union and Asian foreign ministers meeting in Singapore this week to condemn attacks on international humanitarian and rights workers.

Action was needed after the killings of U.N. human rights personnel in Rwanda, the kidnappings of UNCHR workers in Tajikistan and the killing of Red Cross staff in Chechnya, the Brussels office of Human Rights Watch urged in a statement.

"It is critical for all governments to signal their condemnation of these attacks and their determination to protect the lives of humanitarian and human rights workers everywhere," said Lotte Leicht, the group's Brussels director.

Leicht also urged the ministers, who meet on February 13-14, to address other critical issues and back a global initiative to ban land mines, take steps to protect migrant workers from racist violence and push for United Nations access to Burma.

On land mines, the rights group criticised France, Britain, China and South Korea for failing to support a Canadian initiative for a conference in December 1997 that would lead to a treaty banning anti-personnel mines worldwide. On Burma, Leicht said that regular visits by U.N. representatives would be a critical first step in making Burma's military regime more open and in improving human rights.

The group noted that every country at the Asia-Europe meeting faced problems with migrant workers and it urged them to pledge in Singapore to ratify the U.N. Convention on the Rights of all Migrant Workers and Their Families.
Human Rights Watch is a Washington-based international non-governmental organisation founded in 1978 to press for and monitor internationally accepted standards of free society.
